sources.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) Exam Guide, Version 1.1 (October 29, 2026)
sources.note: Domains, weights, task statements, response types, scoring and service lists transcribed from the HTML guide and its sub-pages (domains 1-4, in-scope, out-of-scope, technologies and concepts, revisions). Revisions: 1.0 2026-08-28, 1.1 2026-10-29; AWS publishes updates about a month before they reach the exam. The `scope` arrays are CONDENSED from the guide's 'Knowledge of / Skills in' bullets.

sources.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (certification page)
sources.note: Source of the 130-minute duration, 65-question total and 150 USD price; these are not in the guide. The page announces no successor to SAA-C03.

version.note: No newer version is announced on the certification page or in the guide (checked 2026-11-10). Guide version 1.1 (2026-10-29) should reach the exam about a month after publication.

exam.name: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate
exam.passMarkNote: Official pass mark is a scaled score of 720 on a 100-1000 scale (compensatory scoring: only the overall result matters). The raw-percentage equivalent is not published, so 72% is a PROXY for display on mock results only.
exam.readinessTargetNote: Your own per-exam target for dashboard/map status (default 80%). Not a vendor figure.
exam.timeLimitNote: From the AWS certification page, not the exam guide.
exam.unscoredNote: 15 unscored questions are not identified on the real exam. Unanswered = incorrect; no penalty for guessing.

questionTypes.single: Multiple choice: 1 correct response, 3 distractors (4 options).
questionTypes.multi: Multiple response: 2 or more correct responses out of 5 or more options.

marketing.tagline: Design secure, resilient, fast and cost-aware systems on AWS.
marketing.audience: Builders with about a year of hands-on AWS experience who choose services and shape architectures.
highlights: Security leads at 30%, then resilience (26%), performance (24%) and cost (20%).
Scenario questions: pick the design that meets the requirement with the stated trade-off.
The broadest associate exam here: networking, storage, databases, analytics and migration all appear.

objectives.title: Design secure access to AWS resources
scope: Access controls and management across multiple accounts; security strategy for multiple accounts (AWS Control Tower, SCPs)
Federated access and identity services (IAM, IAM Identity Center); when to federate a directory service with IAM roles
Security best practices for IAM users and the root user (least privilege, MFA)
Flexible authorization model: IAM users, groups, roles and policies
Role-based access control (AWS STS, role switching, cross-account access)
Appropriate use of resource policies for AWS services
AWS global infrastructure (Availability Zones, Regions); the shared responsibility model

objectives.title: Design secure workloads and applications
scope: Application configuration and credentials security; secure application access
AWS service endpoints; controlling ports, protocols and network traffic
VPC security components (security groups, route tables, network ACLs, NAT gateways)
Network segmentation (public and private subnets)
Integrating services to secure applications (AWS Shield, AWS WAF, IAM Identity Center, AWS Secrets Manager)
Security services by use case (Amazon Cognito, Amazon GuardDuty, Amazon Macie)
Threat vectors external to AWS (DDoS, SQL injection)
Securing external network connections (VPN, AWS Direct Connect)

objectives.title: Determine appropriate data security controls
scope: Data access and governance; data retention and classification; aligning with compliance requirements
Encryption at rest (AWS KMS) and in transit (ACM with TLS); key management
Access policies for encryption keys; rotating keys and renewing certificates
Data backups and replication; data recovery
Policies for data access, lifecycle and protection

objectives.title: Design scalable and loosely coupled architectures
scope: Event-driven, microservice and multi-tier architectures; stateless vs stateful workloads
Loose coupling with managed services (Amazon SQS, publish/subscribe, AWS Transfer Family, AWS Secrets Manager)
API creation and management (Amazon API Gateway, REST APIs)
Horizontal vs vertical scaling; scaling strategies per component
Caching strategies; edge accelerators (CDN)
Load balancing (Application Load Balancer)
Containers: when to use them, migrating applications into containers, orchestration (Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS)
Serverless technologies and patterns (AWS Fargate, AWS Lambda); workflow orchestration (AWS Step Functions)
Storage types (object, file, block); when to use read replicas; purpose-built services

objectives.title: Design highly available and/or fault-tolerant architectures
scope: AWS global infrastructure (Availability Zones, Regions, Amazon Route 53); HA across AZs or Regions
Disaster recovery strategies (backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby, active-active failover; RPO and RTO)
Failover strategies; distributed design patterns; mitigating single points of failure
Immutable infrastructure; automation to ensure infrastructure integrity
Load balancing (ALB); proxies (Amazon RDS Proxy); basic networking (route tables)
Service quotas and throttling, including quotas for a standby environment
Durability and availability of data (backups, replication)
Workload visibility (AWS X-Ray); metrics based on business requirements
Improving reliability of legacy applications that cannot be changed; managed services by use case (Amazon Comprehend, Amazon Polly)

objectives.title: Determine high-performing and/or scalable storage solutions
scope: Storage services by use case (Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, Amazon EBS)
Storage types (object, file, block); hybrid storage solutions
Storage configurations that meet performance demands and scale for future needs

objectives.title: Design high-performing and elastic compute solutions
scope: Compute services by use case (AWS Batch, Amazon EMR, AWS Fargate, AWS Lambda)
Container orchestration (Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS); distributed computing and edge services
Scaling (Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling, AWS Auto Scaling); metrics and conditions for scaling actions
Decoupling workloads so components scale independently (queuing, publish/subscribe)
Choosing compute options and sizes (EC2 instance types, Lambda memory)

objectives.title: Determine high-performing database solutions
scope: Database types and services (serverless, relational vs non-relational, in-memory; Amazon Aurora, Amazon DynamoDB)
Data access patterns (read-intensive vs write-intensive); capacity planning (capacity units, instance types, Provisioned IOPS)
Read replicas; database replication
Caching (Amazon ElastiCache); database connections and proxies
Choosing a database engine (MySQL vs PostgreSQL); heterogeneous and homogeneous migrations

objectives.title: Determine high-performing and/or scalable network architectures
scope: Edge networking (Amazon CloudFront, AWS Global Accelerator)
Network design (subnet tiers, routing, IP addressing); topologies (global, hybrid, multi-tier)
Connection options (AWS VPN, AWS Direct Connect, AWS PrivateLink)
Load balancing strategy (Application Load Balancer); placement of resources
Network configurations that scale for future needs

objectives.title: Determine high-performing data ingestion and transformation solutions
scope: Building and securing data lakes (AWS Lake Formation); secure access to ingestion points
Data streaming architectures (Amazon Kinesis); ingestion patterns and frequency
Data transfer solutions (AWS DataSync, AWS Storage Gateway); sizes and speeds
Data transformation (AWS Glue); converting formats such as .csv to .parquet
Analytics and visualization (Amazon Athena, Amazon Quick); compute for processing (Amazon EMR)

objectives.title: Design cost-optimized storage solutions
scope: Storage services by use case and cost (Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, Amazon EBS, Amazon FSx)
Storage tiering and S3 object lifecycles; data lifecycles; access patterns
Block storage options (HDD vs SSD volume types); right-sizing storage; storage auto scaling
Backup and archival solutions
Hybrid storage and transfer (AWS DataSync, AWS Transfer Family, AWS Storage Gateway); lowest-cost transfer to AWS
Access options (S3 Requester Pays); batch vs individual uploads
Cost management features and tools (cost allocation tags, multi-account billing, AWS Cost Explorer, AWS Budgets, AWS Cost and Usage Report)

objectives.title: Design cost-optimized compute solutions
scope: Purchasing options (Spot Instances, Reserved Instances, Savings Plans)
Instance families and sizes (memory optimized, compute optimized)
Cost-effective compute services (AWS Lambda, Amazon EC2, AWS Fargate); containers, serverless and microservices
Scaling strategies (auto scaling, hibernation; horizontal vs vertical)
Load balancer choice (ALB Layer 7, NLB Layer 4, Gateway Load Balancer)
Availability needs by workload class (production vs non-production); hybrid compute (AWS Outposts); edge processing
Cost management features and tools (cost allocation tags, multi-account billing, AWS Cost Explorer, AWS Budgets, AWS Cost and Usage Report)

objectives.title: Design cost-optimized database solutions
scope: Cost-effective database services (DynamoDB vs Amazon RDS, serverless) and types (time series, columnar)
Capacity planning (capacity units); caching; connections and proxies; read replicas
Backup and retention policies (snapshot frequency); data retention
Choosing a database engine (MySQL vs PostgreSQL); migrating schemas and data between locations or engines
Cost management features and tools (cost allocation tags, multi-account billing, AWS Cost Explorer, AWS Budgets, AWS Cost and Usage Report)

objectives.title: Design cost-optimized network architectures
scope: NAT gateways (NAT instance vs NAT gateway costs; one shared NAT gateway vs one per Availability Zone)
Network connections (AWS Direct Connect vs VPN vs internet); bandwidth (one or several VPNs, Direct Connect speed)
Routing to reduce data transfer costs (between Regions and AZs, private vs public, AWS Global Accelerator, VPC endpoints)
Routing, topology and peering (AWS Transit Gateway, VPC peering); DNS
CDNs and edge caching; load balancing (ALB); throttling strategy; reviewing workloads for network savings
Cost management features and tools (cost allocation tags, multi-account billing, AWS Cost Explorer, AWS Budgets, AWS Cost and Usage Report)
